house

noun a building for human habitation, especially one that is lived in by a family or small group of people.

They live in a large house on the edge of town.

noun a building in which people meet for a particular activity.

The local opera house was full for the opening night.

noun a legislative or deliberative assembly.

The bill passed both houses of parliament after a long debate.

verb to provide space for something, to store something.

The gallery houses a fine collection of early paintings.

noun a style of popular dance music with a repetitive beat.

The club played house until the early hours of the morning.
xylophone

noun a percussion instrument with wooden bars of different lengths played with small hammers.
zebra

noun an African wild horse with black-and-white stripes and an erect mane.

A herd of zebras grazed near the river at dusk.
water

noun a clear, colourless liquid that falls as rain and fills rivers, lakes and seas.
whale

noun a very large marine mammal that breathes air through a blowhole on top of its head.

A blue whale surfaced beside the boat.
